label: Late original-phase tokens (x/i/l/h/1/c/v/d) in sequences starting with k/t/j/g/a/p/e/r
explanation: Almost entirely an original-phase unit (99.9% of mass): it fires only at original positions 4-8, with the rate climbing steeply by position (orig_idx 5: 2.5%, 8: 16%), so it is strongest on the last 1-3 tokens before <DEL> in long (L=8-9) sequences. Given that position, the input token matters a lot: x (6.2x lift, largest share of mass and the top activations), then i, l, h, and more weakly 1, c, v, d. It is more active on the first occurrence of a token. History also modulates it: it is more likely to fire when the sequence starts with (or contains early) one of k/t/j/g/a/p/e/r, which looks like a graded bias carried in the hidden state rather than a hard condition. It never fires at t<4, essentially never in the copy phase (0 activations), and only weakly at the delimiter. The predicate (late position x token set x first-token set) gets dev P=0.53 R=0.48 F1=0.51; position alone has recall 0.98 but precision 0.08. Activation looks like a graded sum of position, current token, and prefix-token contributions, so no crisp boolean rule captures it.
